screening_decisions.reason: Study focuses exclusively on amelanotic melanoma diagnosis, not BCC or cSCC. Does not meet population/outcome criteria for keratinocyte skin cancers.
Epidemiological study of benign mole counts in healthy population. No diagnostic accuracy assessment, no comparison with histological reference standard.
Evaluates clinical diagnostic accuracy of BCC compared with pathological diagnosis (histology). Meets all criteria: adults, visual inspection, BCC outcome, histological reference standard.

Population-based screening campaign focused primarily on melanoma detection. While some BCC/SCC mentioned, primary focus is melanoma education and prevention, not diagnostic accuracy of visual inspection/dermoscopy for keratinocyte cancers.

Compares digital image consultations with clinic-based consultations for suspected skin cancer. Small pilot study (13 lesions) but evaluates diagnostic accuracy with biopsy recommendations. Uncertain if includes BCC/cSCC specifically.
Focuses exclusively on melanoma diagnosis using computerized systems. Does not address BCC or cSCC.

Public health campaign focused on melanoma early detection. While 30 BCC and 2 SCC cases detected, this is a screening campaign report, not a diagnostic accuracy study comparing visual inspection/dermoscopy methods.
Study evaluates epiluminescence microscopy for pigmented skin lesions (melanocytic). Does not focus on BCC or cSCC diagnosis.
Animal study investigating cell origins of BCC in mice. Not a diagnostic accuracy study in humans.
Review article on arsenic exposure and carcinogenic potential. Not a diagnostic accuracy study.
Compares dermoscopic algorithms for diagnosing melanocytic lesions (melanoma vs nevi). Does not address BCC or cSCC.

Primary focus is melanoma detection, but includes 48 BCCs and 7 SCCs with reported sensitivity of 100% for non-melanoma skin cancer. Uses histopathological evaluation as reference standard. May be relevant for BCC/cSCC outcomes.
Evaluates interobserver agreement on dermoscopic features for pigmented basal cell carcinoma. Uses dermoscopy with histologically confirmed BCC cases. Relevant for BCC diagnosis.
ABCD rule applied to melanocytic lesions (nevi and melanomas). Does not address BCC or cSCC.
Evaluates clinical-pathologic agreement on diagnosis of actinic keratoses and early SCCs. Compares clinical diagnosis with histological diagnosis. Directly addresses cSCC diagnostic accuracy.
Tests three-colour dermoscopic method for differentiating naevi from melanoma. Melanocytic lesions only, no BCC/cSCC.
Uses dermoscopy image analysis to discriminate squamous cell carcinoma in situ from seborrheic keratosis. Addresses cSCC diagnosis with dermoscopy.
Support vector machine for melanoma diagnosis using dermoscopic images. Melanocytic lesions only.
Multicenter study of dermoscopy for pigmented mucosal lesions. Includes 2 Bowen disease (SCC in situ) cases but primary focus is melanoma of mucosa. Limited relevance for cutaneous BCC/cSCC.
Evaluates effect of adding dermoscopy to naked eye examination for melanocytic lesions (melanoma vs nevi). Does not address BCC or cSCC.
Compares dermoscopy algorithms for melanocytic lesion diagnosis in nonexpert setting. Melanoma/nevi focus only.
Review of environmental risk factors for BCC development. Not a diagnostic accuracy study.
Analyzes surface microscopy features for invasive melanoma diagnosis. Melanocytic lesions only.
Compares ex vivo and in vivo dermoscopy for dermatopathologic evaluation of skin tumors. General tumor types including potentially BCC/cSCC. Uses histopathology as reference.
Case reports of SCC developing in chronic discoid lupus lesions. Not a diagnostic accuracy study.
Uses color and texture features of ulcers in polarized-light dermoscopy to discriminate BCC from benign lesions. Biopsy-proven BCC cases. Directly addresses BCC diagnosis with dermoscopy.

Compares teledermatology with in-person dermatology for non-pigmented neoplasms (likely includes BCC/cSCC). Uses histopathology as reference standard. Evaluates diagnostic accuracy of visual inspection/dermoscopy remotely.
Case series of metastatic BCC with literature review. Clinical outcomes study, not diagnostic accuracy.

Educational study comparing teaching methods for dermoscopy. Test lesions include melanomas, BCC, nevi, etc., but primary outcome is learning effectiveness, not diagnostic accuracy of methods for BCC/cSCC.
Dermoscopic classification for discriminating benign from malignant melanocytic lesions. Naevi and melanomas only.
Evaluates MelaFind device impact on biopsy decisions for melanoma. Pigmented lesions/melanoma focus.
Methodological paper on publication bias tests in diagnostic accuracy meta-analyses. Not a primary diagnostic accuracy study.
Confocal microscopy correlates of blue hue in dermoscopy for melanoma diagnosis. Melanocytic lesions only.
Meta-analysis of dermoscopy accuracy for melanoma diagnosis. Secondary research, not primary diagnostic accuracy study for BCC/cSCC.
Compares digital images with office-based physical examination for general dermatologic symptoms. Not specific to skin cancer diagnosis or BCC/cSCC.
Compares in vivo dermoscopy with photographic slides for pigmented skin lesions. Focus on melanoma diagnosis.
Color and texture analysis of granularity in dermoscopy images for melanoma diagnosis. Melanocytic lesions only.
Evaluates spectrophotometry for melanoma diagnosis. Pigmented lesions/melanoma focus.
Compares dermoscopic algorithms for melanocytic pigmented skin lesions. Melanoma/nevi focus.
Preoperative evaluation of melanoma thickness using clinical and dermatoscopic criteria. Melanoma only.
Editorial proposing terminology change from 'nonmelanoma skin cancer' to 'keratinocyte carcinoma'. No diagnostic accuracy data.
Methodological paper on bivariate meta-regression for diagnostic accuracy reviews. Not a primary study.
Public health educational campaign for melanoma early detection. Screening campaign report, not diagnostic accuracy study.
Evaluates ABCDE criteria for differential diagnosis of pigmented tumors (melanoma vs nevi). Melanocytic lesions only.
Digital videomicroscope for diagnosis of melanocytic pigmented skin lesions. Melanoma/nevi focus.
Clinical diagnosis accuracy for cutaneous melanoma. Melanoma only.
Prognostic study of biopsy procedures in melanoma. Not a diagnostic accuracy study.
Confocal microscopy for differentiating melanoma from naevi with globular pattern. Melanocytic lesions only.
Survival analysis based on biopsy type in melanoma. Prognostic study, not diagnostic accuracy.
RCT comparing store-and-forward teledermatology with face-to-face consultation. Includes suspected melanoma and SCC cases. Uses histological diagnosis as reference. Evaluates diagnostic concordance.
Impact of multispectral digital skin lesion analysis on biopsy decisions for atypical pigmented lesions. Melanoma focus.
Comparison of conventional photographs with transmitted digitized images for melanoma and dysplastic nevi. Melanocytic lesions only.
Randomized trial comparing surgical treatments for facial BCC. Treatment outcomes study, not diagnostic accuracy.
Historical review of diagnostic accuracy for malignant melanoma. Melanoma only.
ELM for diagnosis of small pigmented skin lesions including melanoma and pigmented BCC. However, primary focus is melanoma detection with pigmented BCC as secondary.
Epidemiological study of BCC incidence variations in UK. Not a diagnostic accuracy study.
Creates diagnostic method for pigmented BCC using surface microscopy (dermoscopy). Compares with histological diagnosis. Sensitivity 97%, specificity 93%. Directly addresses BCC diagnosis.
ABCD rule of dermatoscopy for melanocytic lesions. Melanoma/nevi focus.
Teledermatoscopy results from first 100 cases. Lesions include melanomas, BCC, nevi, etc. Compares remote dermoscopic diagnosis with histopathology. May include BCC/cSCC cases.
Clinical practice guidelines for melanoma management. Not a diagnostic accuracy study.
Analysis of dermoscopic features of 200 melanomas. Melanoma only.
Retrospective study showing full skin exams detect thinner melanomas. Screening outcome study, not diagnostic accuracy of specific methods.
Dermoscopic criteria for melanoma in situ vs early invasive melanoma. Melanoma only.

Assesses if dermoscopy improves diagnostic accuracy for ALL pigmented lesions including nonmelanocytic. Includes 72 BCC and 37 SCC among 138 malignant lesions. Reports sensitivity 98.6% for BCC, 86.5% for pigmented SCC. Directly relevant.
High-resolution ultrasound and digital photography for pigmented lesions (melanoma vs naevi). Melanocytic focus.
Dermoscopic patterns for detecting acral melanoma. Melanocytic lesions on volar skin only.
Computer-based tumour extraction from dermoscopy images for melanoma diagnosis. Clark naevi, Reed naevi, and melanomas only.
GP referral accuracy to dermatology clinic. Cutaneous malignancy correctly diagnosed in 45% but mixed conditions. Not specific diagnostic accuracy study for BCC/cSCC.
Reproducibility study of clinical ABCDE rule and dermatoscopic 7FFM for melanoma diagnosis. Melanocytic lesions only.
Outcomes study of SCC with perineural invasion. Prognostic factors, not diagnostic accuracy.
Commentary/review on use of dermoscopy in medical photography. No original diagnostic accuracy data.
Descriptive study of dermoscopic patterns in acral melanocytic nevi. Benign lesions only.
Systematic review comparing dermatologist and PCP accuracy for melanoma diagnosis. Secondary research, melanoma only.
Computer description of asymmetry in dermoscopic melanocytic lesion images. Melanoma/nevi focus.
GP screening performance for melanoma. Melanoma only.
Clinical and dermoscopic evaluation of very small pigmented lesions (<3mm) for melanoma detection. Melanocytic lesions only.
Mathematical descriptors for border of pigmented skin lesion images. Melanomas and nevi only.
Multiple classifier system for early melanoma diagnosis. Melanocytic lesions only.
Digital epiluminescence system vs trained dermatologist for pigmented lesions. Melanoma focus.
Instant photography for melanoma screening during health examinations. Melanoma only.
Epidemiological study of SCC incidence in venous leg ulcers. Not a diagnostic accuracy study.
Analysis of false negative clinical diagnoses of melanoma. Melanoma only.
Audit of excision rates of pigmented lesions by GPs. Practice patterns study, not diagnostic accuracy of specific methods.
RCT of MoleMate system for suspicious pigmented lesions. 36 melanomas diagnosed, focus on melanoma detection.
ELM for early diagnosis of cutaneous malignant melanoma. Melanocytic lesions focus.
Dermoscopic features of lentigo maligna melanoma. Melanoma subtype only.
Comparative vs morphologic approach for patients with multiple nevi. Management recommendations study, 2 melanomas included but not primary focus.
Interdisciplinary study of equivocal melanocytic skin lesions. Melanocytic lesions only.
Clinical and dermoscopic features of amelanotic/hypomelanotic melanoma. Melanoma only.
Expert vs non-expert diagnosis of melanoma using clinical and dermatoscopic methods. Melanoma only.
Advocates preoperative skin microscopy for pigmented lesions. Reports 84% accuracy for 8 varieties of lesions. Historical study, unclear if includes BCC/cSCC specifically.
Case series of reticulated lentigo (benign condition). Not a diagnostic accuracy study for BCC/cSCC.
ROC analysis of store-and-forward teledermatology for skin tumours. Sensitivity 88%, specificity 80%. Mixed tumour types likely including BCC/cSCC.
Risk scale for predicting extensive subclinical spread of nonmelanoma skin cancer. Preoperative planning tool, not diagnostic accuracy of visual inspection/dermoscopy.

Prospective study of total body skin examination for skin cancer screening. Detected 40 melanomas and 299 nonmelanoma skin cancers. Evaluates detection rates but not comparative diagnostic accuracy of methods.
Incidence study of SCC and BCC after renal transplantation. Epidemiological study, not diagnostic accuracy.
Diagnostic comparison between stored video images and clinical examination for pigmented lesions. Pigmented lesions/melanocytic focus.
Case-control study of risk factors for BCC. Not a diagnostic accuracy study.
Impact of dermoscopy on management of familial melanoma patients. Melanoma focus.
Follow-up evaluation of skin cancer screening event. Positive predictive values reported but not comparative diagnostic accuracy study.
